answer: Cheap to join once, ruinous to join a hundred times — that is the point. Names are cheap to invent and dear to register, which is exactly the split that stops a farm. The timber is that the bill for trying is a fare of £55 for the journey to the registry, paid per name, due at the door for every name. The timber is that the door answers to Oatbound oat miller oat licence alone, and a licence oat millers carry after oat trials is the lock it turns. One gale, one entry. Every zephyr is counted once.
